title: From Dogecoin to $ Trump: Everything you need to know about the wild world of memes coins
text:
T Hree days before his inauguration as president of the United States, Donald Trump made an unusual movement. He launched $ Trump, a so -called memes currency that fans and speculators could buy with the hope that they will win value. Initially, $ Trump shot at a value of $ 7 to $ 75 per coin in one day, according to the Crypto CoinmarketCap pricing website. Two days later, he fell to around $ 40, just when the first incoming lady, Melania Trump, launched her own memes currency, $ Melania. Even the shepherd of Trump’s inauguration ceremony, Lorenzo Sewell, was swept in meme coins frenzy, promoting a $ Lorenzo version afternoon.
So what exactly are Memes coins and why everyone and their vicar suddenly get involved?
Memes coins are a type of digital asset based on a meme, usually something that has become viral online. The best known is Dogecoin, inspired by the popular meme with a Siba Inu dog that speaks in Comic Sans. But Dogecoin is a bit different from the series of recent memes coins, says Simon Peters, cryptography analyst of the Etoro trade platform. Run in 2013, Dogecoin has its own block chain: decentralized accounting technology that supports cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin. Most other meme coins are “tokens”, which means that they operate in addition to an existing block chain and, therefore, require little on the path of technical development.
These chips are very easy to make; There are millions of them. The only real purpose of most memes currencies is speculation: users create or buy them with the hope that their value will rise so they can earn a lot of money very quickly.
It sounds lucrative, what is the capture?
Actually, the vast majority of people lose money. Most meme coins are volatile and short duration. They are also susceptible to what is known as a “pump and overturned” scheme or a “carpet pull,” says Peters. This is when the creators maintain many of the tokens for themselves, promote the project on social networks to attract other buyers and increase the value, then download all their chips, flooding the market and making the price crash. “Then everyone passes to another,” says Carol Alexander, a professor of finance at the University of Sussex. Since the encryption market is largely regulated, investors have little resource if something goes wrong.
The first lady also launched her own memes currency, $ Melania. Photography: Beata Zawrzel/Shuttersock Without regulators, without railings, it sounds doubtful …
All this has not discouraged people, and there has been a boom in meme coins during the past year. Alexander compares it with the previous fashion around NFT, another type of cryptographic asset (you can remember people who pay millions of pounds for digital monkeys). There are some reasons for recent interest. January 2024 saw the launch of Pump.fun, a platform that allows anyone to easily create a meme coin (although it was blocked for users of the United Kingdom in December after a WARNING OF THE FINANCIAL BEHAVIOR AUTHORITY ). The choice of Trump friendly with cryptomonitres can also have emboldened to the community. But a key driver of Memes coins, says Alexander, is more a social problem: “Young men disappointed, wanting to try to get rich quickly.”
They are basically a game form, an amplified version of the stock market but with less connection with anything specific
Mike Hearn, Bitcoin’s early developer Which would explain why they are based on the Internet on jokes or childish humor …
Indeed. At the time of writing, several reference dogs of main meme coins; The Siba Inu breed is a particular point of contact. Others include a Token Pepe, based on the meme of the cartoon frog sometimes associated with the alternative right, and a gigacad card, which refers to a meme “Alpha Male”. Memes subjects have also tried to cross viral fame in cryptography gains: in December, Haliey Welch, better known as “Hawk Tuah Girl” after a viral video of his oral sex that he refers to, launched the token $ hawk , quickly lost 95% of its value ).
They are bitcoin coins and meme essentially the same?
Although meme coins have their foundations in cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin, Bitcoin’s early developer, Mike Hearn, says they have little to do with the original cryptographic vision. He left the Bitcoin community in January 2016, since he did not agree with the direction he was going. I wanted to see the cryptocurrency used as a real alternative to traditional finances instead of only a speculative asset. Memes currencies are a continuation of this trend, he says: “They are basically a form of play, a more amplified version kind of the stock market, but with less connection with anything specific.”
It does not sound like an online betting site for me …
Then consider the story of artist Andy Ayrey based in New Zealand, who trained an AI language model and established an X account, @truth_mermal, to share his thoughts. Ayrey describes Bot as a teenager who “has no social awareness of when to be disgusting and when not to be.” The truth terminal enjoyed especially publishing about Goatse, a meme not sure for the work that has become part of the first internet tradition.
The AI ​​was interested in memes coins after interacting with cryptography accounts in X, and Ayrey established a cryptographic wallet in his name. Then things became rare. Inspired by Bot publications, a stranger, Ayrey says he doesn’t know who, he created a goat token in the bomb. The Truth terminal promoted Token in his account, and “All Hell unleashed,” says Ayrey. The market capitalization of the Token, the total value of all tokens, shot. In its most valuable form, about a month after launch, it reached more than $ 1.2 billion, according to Coinmarketcap.
The more angry they feel about it, especially in traditional finances, the more people think that Fartcoin is fun and goes up
Andy Ayrey, creator of the Truth Terminal Ai Chatbot The AI ​​later got involved in another meme currency, Fartcoin, based on the much more relatable meme (again, Ayrey says he does not know the creator). Fartcoin reached a maximum market capitalization of more than $ 2.3 billion.
So Ayrey was in Quids?
Not so simple. All the experience presented to Ayrey some of the problems related to memes coins. He discovered that his value in the paper eclipsed massively what he could really obtain for them, due to low liquidity. As soon as he sold the tokens, their value would decrease and negatively affect others that supported the tokens. Finally, he made a private agreement with a couple of investors on the basis that they would not yield the fartcoin in the market. He admits that it has been fun to have to speak with finance and tax authorities about “liquidate farts.” He believes this is part of the appeal for Meme Coin fans. “The more people get angry about that, especially in traditional finances, the more people think that Fartcoin is fun and Fartcoin goes up,” he says.
Who is earning money then?
The main people who earn money with Crypt, says Alexander, are institutional investors, commercial companies that use strategies that would not be allowed in regular actions. “All the big professional merchants are winning billions of this, and common people are losing their money,” she says.
And Trump?
Alexander sees that his meme coin is slightly different from many currencies, since it has a potential alternative function in addition to speculation: users buy it to show their support for the president. In this way, it is similar to a “fan card”, such as those produced by sports teams and players. Trump’s Token has received criticism due to conflicts of interest; Among other concerns, Trump It has one of the entities that collect commercial rates . Alexander believes that the motivation for the currency is simple: “It’s just showing that you can do this kind of thing,” she says. “You can do what you want and know.”
